cards.front: Why does a gas exert pressure on the walls of its container?
cards.back: Gas particles constantly strike the walls, and each **collision** exerts a force on the wall. The combined force per unit area is the **pressure**.
cards.hint: Think about what the particles are doing when they meet the wall.

cards.front: What does the temperature of a gas tell you about its particles?
cards.back: **Temperature** is linked to the average kinetic energy of the particles. A higher temperature means the particles move faster on average.

cards.front: Why does heating a gas in a sealed rigid container raise its pressure?
cards.back: Its particles move faster on average, so they strike the walls more often and exert greater force in each impact. This raises the force per unit area, so the **pressure** rises.
cards.hint: Start with what heating does to particle speed.

cards.front: What is meant by random motion of gas particles?
cards.back: **Random motion** is movement in constantly changing directions, with no single direction followed by all the particles.

cards.front: What does the average speed of gas particles describe?
cards.back: The **average speed** describes the motion of the particles as a group. It does not mean every particle travels at that speed.
cards.hint: Think about whether all particles move at the same speed.

cards.front: Why do gas particles reach every part of their container?
cards.back: Their **random motion** and collisions carry them through all the available space. Gas particles are far apart, so they have room to move throughout.
cards.hint: Compare how far apart gas particles are with particles in solids.

cards.front: What is pressure in terms of force?
cards.back: **Pressure** is the force exerted per unit area of a surface.

cards.front: Where does gas pressure act inside a container?
cards.back: Pressure acts on every inside surface of the container, not just the bottom.

cards.front: Why is it wrong to say temperature gives the speed of one particular particle?
cards.back: Temperature describes the gas as a whole, linked to the **average** kinetic energy. Individual particles still have different speeds.

cards.front: What is a sealed rigid container?
cards.back: A **sealed rigid container** stops gas escaping and keeps its volume fixed.

cards.front: Why might heating a gas in a flexible container not raise its pressure in the same way?
cards.back: The container can expand, increasing the gas volume. This can reduce how often particles strike each area of wall, so the **pressure** may not rise as it does in a rigid container.
cards.hint: Compare what can happen to the volume in each type of container.
